examples.problem: What is the coefficient of $(x-1)^3$ in the third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x) = e^{-2x}?$
examples.worked_solution:
The coefficient of $(x-1)^3$ is $\dfrac{1}{3!}f^{(3)}(1).$ Let's compute the necessary derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={e}^{-2x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-2{e}^{-2x} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =4{e}^{-2x} \\ {f}^{(3)}(x) & =-8{e}^{-2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{1}{3!}f^{(3)}(1) =\dfrac{1}{6} \left( -8e^{-2} \right) = -\dfrac{4}{3e^2}.
$$

So the coefficient of $(x-1)^3$ is $-\dfrac{4}{3e^2}.$

feedback.problem: The third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)$ about $x=0$ is
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the third-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=0,$ we plug $a=0$ into the general formula to give

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)x+{f}^{″}(0)\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+{f}^{‴}(0)\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!} \\  & =f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)x+{f}^{″}(0)\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{f}^{‴}(0)\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We need to compute $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ ${f}^{″}(0),$ and ${f}^{‴}(0),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & ⟹ &  & f(0) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡0=1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(0) & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡0=0 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-9\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(0) & =-9\operatorname{cos}⁡0=-9 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =27\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(0) & =27\operatorname{sin}⁡0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we plug the results for $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ ${f}^{″}(0),$ and ${f}^{‴}(0)$ into our third-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =1+0\cdot x-9\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+0\cdot \frac{{x}^{3}}{6} \\  & =1-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
